topicDisplay: Paper 1: Non-fiction Texts and Transactional Writing
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Paper 1: format, marks and assessment objectives

questions.q: What percentage of the total Edexcel International GCSE English Language (Spec A) qualification is Paper 1 worth?
questions.explain: Paper 1: Non-fiction Texts and Transactional Writing accounts for 60% of the qualification, with Paper 2 making up the remaining 40%.

questions.q: How long is the Paper 1 written examination?
questions.explain: Paper 1 is a 2 hour 15 minute written examination covering both the reading and writing sections.

questions.q: What is the total number of marks available on Paper 1?
questions.explain: Paper 1 is marked out of 90, split evenly as 45 marks for Section A (Reading) and 45 marks for Section B (Writing).

questions.q: Which assessment objective focuses on analysing how writers use linguistic and structural devices to achieve effects and influence readers?
questions.explain: AO2 assesses understanding and analysis of how writers use language and structure to create effects, whereas AO1 covers selecting and interpreting information.

questions.q: Which pair of assessment objectives is used to mark the transactional writing task in Section B?
questions.explain: Writing is assessed through AO4 (communicating effectively and adapting form, tone and register) and AO5 (clear, accurate expression, structure and spelling, punctuation and grammar).

questions.q: Who is the author of the anthology non-fiction text 'A Passage to Africa'?
questions.explain: 'A Passage to Africa' is an autobiographical account by the journalist George Alagiah.

questions.q: Which writer wrote the anthology piece 'Young and dyslexic? You've got it going on'?
questions.explain: This motivational article about living with dyslexia was written by the poet Benjamin Zephaniah.

questions.q: The anthology extract 'Between a Rock and a Hard Place' was written by which author?
questions.explain: 'Between a Rock and a Hard Place' is Aron Ralston's autobiographical account of being trapped by a boulder while canyoneering.

questions.q: The anthology text 'Chinese Cinderella' by Adeline Yen Mah is best described as which type of non-fiction?
questions.explain: 'Chinese Cinderella' is an autobiographical extract in which Adeline Yen Mah recounts her own childhood experiences.

questions.q: 'The Danger of a Single Story' by Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie originated in which form?
questions.explain: 'The Danger of a Single Story' is the transcript of a talk (a TED talk) delivered by Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie.

questions.q: 'Explorers, or boys messing about? Either way, the taxpayer gets rescue bill' is an example of which non-fiction text type?
questions.explain: This anthology piece is a newspaper article reporting on the rescue of two explorers and questioning who should pay.

questions.q: How many texts does a student read and answer questions on in Section A (Reading) of Paper 1?
questions.explain: Section A presents two non-fiction texts: one drawn from the anthology and one previously unseen text.

questions.q: In Section A, Text One is taken from the anthology. What is the source of Text Two?
options: A fiction extract from a novel
questions.explain: Text Two is a previously unseen non-fiction text that candidates have not studied in advance.

questions.q: The final comparison question in Section A typically asks candidates to compare what across the two texts?
options: How the two writers present their ideas, perspectives and use of language
The rhyme schemes and metre of the two texts
The characters and plot of the two stories
The spelling and punctuation of the two writers
questions.explain: The comparison question requires candidates to explore how both writers present ideas and perspectives and how these are conveyed through language and structure.

questions.q: Which statement best defines transactional writing?
options: Purely imaginative writing with no real audience
Writing that serves a real-world purpose for a specific audience
Writing that must always take the form of a narrative story
Writing that consists only of poetry and verse
questions.explain: Transactional writing is non-fiction writing with a real purpose and a defined audience, such as letters, articles, reports, reviews and speeches.

questions.q: In Section B (Transactional Writing), how many tasks must the candidate complete?
options: One task from a choice of two
Two tasks from a choice of four
questions.explain: Candidates complete a single transactional writing task chosen from two options, worth 45 marks.

questions.q: A task asks you to 'write a letter to your local council urging them to build a new skate park in your town'. What is the main purpose of this writing?
questions.explain: Urging the council to take action shows the primary purpose is to persuade the reader towards a particular viewpoint.

questions.q: You are asked to write an article for your school magazine advising students on how to cope with exam stress. Which tone and register is most appropriate?
options: Clear, engaging and suited to a student audience
questions.explain: Adapting tone and register to the audience (AO4) means writing clearly and engagingly for fellow students reading a school magazine.

questions.q: For a speech persuading classmates to recycle more, which technique would be most effective?
options: Rhetorical questions and direct address to the audience
Stanza breaks and a regular rhyme scheme
questions.explain: Rhetorical questions and direct address ('you') engage listeners and are well-suited persuasive devices for a spoken speech.

questions.q: You are asked to write a report for your headteacher about improving the school canteen. Which set of features best fits this form?
options: A formal, structured layout with an objective tone and possible headings
questions.explain: A report to a headteacher requires a formal register, clear structure and an objective tone appropriate to its purpose and audience.
